pool.baseline: I've been thinking a lot about the concept of the 'Sunk Cost Fallacy' in the context of human existence. We're taught that persistence is a virtue, but if you look at it through a strictly rational lens, continuing to maintain a life that yields nothing but diminishing returns—socially, emotionally, even cognitively—starts to look less like resilience and more like an irrational commitment to a failing system. If the 'utility' of one's existence has hit a permanent deficit, isn't the most logical, autonomous move to simply terminate the process? It feels like we're just clinging to a habit out of fear of the void, rather than any actual reason to stay.
